sources.title: Wael Sawan: board biography
sources.findings: Read current Shell board biography: Lebanese and Canadian nationality, CEO since 1 January 2023, initial engineering role with Petroleum Development Oman, MEng and MBA. Its mid-2000s description of Qatar leadership conflicts with contemporaneous reporting; that date is not adopted. Generic corporate praise is not repeated as an independent assessment.

sources.title: 15 September 2022: Who is Shell’s new CEO Sawan?
sources.findings: Read Reuters 15 September 2022 factbox: born in Beirut in July 1974, grew up in Dubai, chemical-engineering master’s. Birth precision remains month, not an invented day. Its November 2021 description of the gas role is superseded by the precise 25 October date in the annual report.

sources.publisher: Shell / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.title: 17 January 2019: appointment as Upstream Director
sources.findings: Read 17 January 2019 appointment filing: Upstream Director and Executive Committee membership effective 1 July 2019; Andy Brown leaves later. The OBE paragraph refers to Brown, not Sawan. Do not transfer that award or confuse Executive Committee membership with appointment to the corporate board.

sources.title: 20 May 2015: Michiel Kool succeeds Sawan in Qatar
sources.findings: Read original report published 20 May 2015, despite a 2022 update timestamp. It places Qatar work from 2008, top-role promotion in April 2012 and appointment to Deepwater in 2015. July 1 is Kool’s succession date; no unsupported precise Deepwater start day is assigned. Kool’s mining degree and career are not Sawan’s.

sources.publisher: Shell / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.title: 2021 annual report, printed page 130: senior management
sources.findings: Read 2021 annual report, printed page 130: Sawan succeeded Wetselaar on 25 October 2021 as Integrated Gas, Renewables and Energy Solutions Director. Tenure from July 2019 concerns Executive Committee service, not continuous tenure in the gas role. Yujnovich’s biography is separate.

sources.publisher: Shell / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.title: 15 September 2022: CEO succession effective 1 January 2023
sources.findings: Read 15 September 2022 SEC announcement: CEO and board appointment effective 1 January 2023. Van Beurden’s later advisory period and June 2023 group departure are not treated as Sawan’s start date.

sources.title: 14 March 2024: Energy Transition Strategy 2024
sources.findings: Read the 14 March 2024 strategy text and target tables. Net carbon intensity by 2030 has a 2016 baseline and 15–20% reduction target; 2035 45% target retired. The separate 15–20% ambition for customers’ use of oil products has a 2021 baseline. Neither is an already-achieved absolute emissions reduction.

sources.title: 14 March 2024: Shell scales back carbon intensity targets
sources.findings: Read Reuters 14 March 2024 report: prior intensity target was 20%; strategy emphasised higher returns, steady oil output and gas growth. Preserve the distinction between intensity and total emissions. These historical target revisions are not claimed to exhaust all strategy updates through 2026.

sources.publisher: Crown Prince Diwan, State of Kuwait
sources.title: 4 November 2026: Crown Prince receives Shell CEO
sources.findings: Read Kuwait Crown Prince Diwan’s dated account of the actual meeting on 4 November 2026 at Bayan Palace. It identifies Sawan as Shell CEO and discussion of economic cooperation. No specific contract or transaction completion is inferred.

sources.title: Notable alumni: Wael Sawan, MEng 1997
sources.findings: Read McGill’s notable-alumni entry, which explicitly lists Sawan as MEng 1997. MBA supported by Shell filing; no unsupported MBA graduation year or engineering doctorate added.
